zh.principle:
**定理**：Goldreich-Levin 定理（Goldreich-Levin Theorem）。### 内积是任何单向函数的硬核位

设 f:{0,1}^n→{0,1}^{m(n)} 是单向函数。把输入写成 (p,x)，|p|=|x|=n，定义
g(p,x) = (p, f(x)),  b(p,x) = p·x mod 2 = Σ_i p_i x_i mod 2。Goldreich–Levin 定理说：b 是 g 的硬核谓词。即使已知 p 与 f(x)，任何多项式时间算法预测 b 的优势都不可忽略地小，除非它能求逆 f。### 预测优势的形式

若 A 满足
Pr[A(p,f(x)) = b(p,x)] ≥ 1/2 + ε(n)
且 ε 不可忽略，则存在概率多项式时间求逆器 B，运行时间 poly(n,1/ε)，以 poly(ε) 的概率从 f(x) 恢复 x。
zh.why:
RSA 的最低位、离散对数的某些位有各自的具体硬核证明；GL 给的是通用结论：任何单向函数都能长出硬核位。它把“隐藏一个比特”从具体假设提升为一般定理。### 它是 HILL 的第一步

GL 提供一位计算熵；HILL 把这些位、单向函数迭代与通用哈希组合成伪随机生成器。没有 GL，OWF→PRG 的链条就缺第一块。
zh.used: - 硬核位：在 f(x) 公开后仍隐藏 x 的一个线性函数，可用于构造 PRG、承诺和零知识中的隐藏挑战。- PRG：反复调用单向函数并提取硬核位，再用混合论证证明输出不可预测；这是 Blum–Micali 生成器的通用化思路。- 归约：把“预测内积”的对手变成“求逆 f”的算法；这是 OWF 到 PRG 证明中的标准一步。
zh.broken:
1.只给一位。每次调用只隐藏一个比特，不能直接当流密码。2.需要长度保持或填充。原定理对 f(p,x)=(p,g(x)) 形式陈述；一般 f 要先规范化。3.损失是 poly(1/ε)。若预测优势 ε=2^{-n/2}，求逆时间可能达到 2^{n/2}，不再多项式。4.只对均匀随机的 p 成立。若 p 的分布可预测，内积的隐藏性不自动成立。5.不给出具体 OWF 的显式硬核位；对具体方案仍要单独证明或选用已知硬核位。### 不等于“任何位都难预测”

GL 说的是内积这一位，不是 f(x) 的每一位。单向函数可能泄漏大量位；硬核位是经过挑选的、与 f(x) 联合分布仍隐藏的位。
zh.history:
Goldreich 与 Levin 在 STOC 1989 证明“所有单向函数都有硬核谓词”，回应 Levin 此前关于内积的猜想。证明使用 Hadamard 码的列表解码：把预测器当成带噪的码字访问，恢复 x 的候选表。### 后续

HILL 1999 把 GL 与通用哈希结合，得到 OWF→PRG；后续工作改进了列表解码效率与具体参数。GL 仍是理论构造，不是实用随机数发生器。

**技术参数与复算边界**

该条目的形式模型是 \(\Pr[\mathrm{Bad}_A(\lambda)]\le \varepsilon(\lambda)\)。输入：输入：Goldreich-Levin 定理的公开参数、密钥/随机数与消息；变量说明：Bad 为归约中定义的失败事件，ε 为可忽略函数。 预期输出：按 Goldreich-Levin 定理 的规范执行后得到可验证的输出或可比较的优势界。 复算必须给出输入、步骤、输出和单位；示例只演示流程，不替代标准测试向量。

en.principle:
**Theorem**: Goldreich-Levin Theorem (Goldreich-Levin 定理). ### The inner product is a hard-core bit for any OWF

Let f:{0,1}^n→{0,1}^{m(n)} be a one-way function. Write the input as (p,x) with |p|=|x|=n and define
g(p,x) = (p, f(x)),  b(p,x) = p·x mod 2 = Σ_i p_i x_i mod 2. The Goldreich–Levin theorem says b is a hard-core predicate for g. Even given p and f(x), every polynomial-time algorithm has negligible advantage in predicting b unless it can invert f. ### The prediction advantage

If A satisfies
Pr[A(p,f(x)) = b(p,x)] ≥ 1/2 + ε(n)
with non-negligible ε, then a probabilistic polynomial-time inverter B exists, running in time poly(n,1/ε), that recovers x from f(x) with probability poly(ε).
en.why:
The least significant bit of RSA and particular bits of discrete log have their own concrete hard-core proofs; GL gives a generic result: every one-way function has a hard-core bit. It lifts “hide one bit” from a specific assumption to a general theorem.

GL supplies one bit of computational entropy; HILL combines these bits, OWF iteration and universal hashing into a pseudorandom generator. Without GL, the OWF→PRG chain lacks its first block.
en.used:
- Hard-core bit: after f(x) is public, a linear function of x remains hidden; it can build PRGs, commitments and hidden challenges in zero knowledge. - PRG: iterate the OWF and extract hard-core bits, then use a hybrid argument to show unpredictability; this generalizes the Blum–Micali generator. - Reduction: turn a predictor of the inner product into an algorithm that inverts f; this is a standard step in OWF-to-PRG proofs.

Reading: fix f and the input length, check that p and x have equal length; if f is not length-preserving, pad first.

A shared name may belong to an algorithm, standard, event, person or term; this entry is responsible only for its catalogue binding and does not absorb adjacent records. If versions, regions or institutions define the name differently, the differences stay side by side.
en.broken:
1. One bit only. Each call hides a single bit; it is not a stream cipher by itself. 2. Length-preserving or padded. The original theorem is stated for f(p,x)=(p,g(x)); a general f must be normalized. 3. The loss is poly(1/ε). If ε=2^{-n/2}, inversion may take 2^{n/2}, no longer polynomial. 4. Only uniform random p. If p’s distribution is predictable, the inner product’s hiding property does not follow automatically. 5. No explicit hard-core bit for a concrete OWF; a concrete scheme still needs its own proof or a known hard-core bit.

GL is about the inner product, not every bit of f(x). A OWF may leak many bits; a hard-core bit is chosen so that its joint distribution with f(x) still hides it.
en.history:
Goldreich and Levin proved at STOC 1989 that every one-way function has a hard-core predicate, answering Levin’s earlier conjecture about the inner product. The proof uses list decoding of the Hadamard code: treat the predictor as noisy codeword access and recover a candidate list for x.

HILL 1999 combined GL with universal hashing to obtain OWF→PRG; later work improved list-decoding efficiency and concrete parameters. GL remains a theoretical construction, not a practical random-number generator.
